Is there a way, in Windows, using tkinter and the Text widget, to have a double-click select with boundaries like ()[],-... along with just space?

Yes. The easiest and most reliable way is to override the Text widget's double-click behavior with your own handler that finds the "word" boundaries you want and then sets the selection. Bind <Double-Button-1> to a callback, compute the token under the click (treating e.g. (), [], comma, hyphen, period and space as separators), add the "sel" tag, and return "break" so Tk's default double-click handling doesn't run.

Example — this treats space, parentheses, brackets, comma, hyphen and dot as separators:

import tkinter as tk
import re

# characters you want to treat as separators: ()[],-. and whitespace
word_re = re.compile(r"[^()\[\],\.\-\s]+")

def select_token(event):
    # get index of click
    idx = text.index("@%d,%d" % (event.x, event.y))
    line_no, col = map(int, idx.split('.'))
    # get the full line
    line = text.get(f"{line_no}.0", f"{line_no}.end")
    # find the token that contains the clicked column
    for m in word_re.finditer(line):
        if m.start() <= col < m.end():
            start = f"{line_no}.{m.start()}"
            end   = f"{line_no}.{m.end()}"
            text.tag_remove("sel", "1.0", "end")
            text.tag_add("sel", start, end)
            text.mark_set("insert", end)
            text.see("insert")
            break
    else:
        # optional: if click on a separator, select that single char
        if 0 <= col < len(line):
            start = f"{line_no}.{col}"
            end   = f"{line_no}.{col+1}"
            text.tag_remove("sel", "1.0", "end")
            text.tag_add("sel", start, end)
    return "break"   # stop default handler

root = tk.Tk()
text = tk.Text(root, wrap="none")
text.pack(expand=1, fill="both")
text.insert("end", "Example: word1(word2),word-3...end")
text.bind("<Double-Button-1>", select_token)
root.mainloop()

Notes and variations
- Adjust the regex pattern to change which characters are treated as separators. For example, include/exclude apostrophes, underscores, Unicode letters, etc.
- If you want to preserve other default bindings (e.g. triple-click selection for a line) you can leave those alone — this only overrides the double-click.
- Returning "break" prevents the default Tk selection. If you omit it you will fight with the default behavior.
- This is cross-platform; no special Windows-only APIs are needed.

If you'd like, tell me the exact characters you want included/excluded (or whether hyphenated words should be treated as a single token), and I can give a tuned regex.
